newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chubais scorns bid to unseat Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: Chubais scorns bid to unseat Yeltsin.

text.p: Boris Yeltsin's chief of staff on Wednesday dismissed as a "political farce" a leading communist politician's attempt to force the president to step down over his ill health.

"The absurdity of this initiative was obvious from the very beginning, both from the legal and the commonsense point of view," Anatoly Chubais told Interfax news agency, referring to a motion by parliament's security committee chief Viktor Ilyukhin.
Ilyukhin is pressing for the lower house of parliament or Duma to vote on Friday on the motion to dismiss Yeltsin, 65, who has been in hospital for a week with pneumonia.
Yeltsin was out of the Kremlin for nearly six months last year with heart problems.
The Russian constitution is vague in describing the removal of a president for health reasons, and the initiative has virtually no chance of success.
The Duma's legal department said on Wednesday that such a motion would carry no legal weight.
"The Duma's main security specialist made a bit of a fool of himself," Chubais told reporters.

He said he had discussed the opposition's moves with Yeltsin on Tuesday in 40 minutes of talks in the Moscow hospital where the president is being treated. The discussion also touched on staffing and regional issues.

"It would have been a normal conversation if it had not taken place in the Central Clinical Hospital, which is of course a great pity. But nevertheless the president is up to date with all our current problems," Chubais said.
